topic: Direct and Indirect Taxes of Economics
description: A tax is a compulsory financial charge imposed by the government to fund public expenditures. The taxation system is primarily classified into Direct Taxes, where the burden cannot be shifted, and Indirect Taxes, where the ultimate burden is shifted to the final consumer.

sections.title: Basic Concepts of Taxation
sections.description: Fundamental terms required to understand the difference between direct and indirect taxes.

key_concepts.explanation: The point where the tax is initially imposed. It refers to the person or entity who is legally liable to pay the tax to the government in the first instance.
The final resting place or the ultimate monetary burden of the tax. In a Direct Tax, the impact and incidence fall on the same person, whereas in an Indirect Tax, they fall on different persons.
A tax that is borne directly by the entity or individual on whom it is imposed (e.g., Income Tax). Its burden cannot be shifted to anyone else.
A tax levied on goods and services. The initial payer of the tax shifts the ultimate economic burden to the final consumer (e.g., GST).

sections.title: Major Direct Taxes
sections.description: Crucial direct taxes levied by the government and their operational definitions.

key_concepts.explanation: A progressive tax levied annually on the income earned by individuals, Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs), and other entities.
A direct tax levied on the net income or profit of corporate entities and companies. It is one of the largest sources of tax revenue for the Government of India.
A tax levied on the profit derived from the sale of a capital asset like property, gold, or shares. It is categorized into short-term and long-term capital gains.
A direct tax levied on the purchase and sale of qualifying securities (like equities and derivatives) listed on recognized stock exchanges in India.

sections.title: Indirect Taxes and GST
sections.description: An overview of the Goods and Services Tax and other prominent indirect taxes.

key_concepts.explanation: A comprehensive, multi-stage, destination-based indirect tax levied on the manufacture, sale, and consumption of goods and services at a national level.
A tax imposed on the import and export of goods across international borders. It remains outside the purview of GST.
A tax levied on the manufacturing or production of goods within the country. While mostly subsumed by GST, it still applies to items like petroleum and alcohol.

historical_events.significance: India completely overhauled its indirect taxation system under the motto 'One Nation, One Tax, One Market'.

sections.title: Constitutional Provisions of Taxation
sections.description: Key articles in the Indian Constitution that govern the imposition and collection of taxes.

polity_articles.provision: Taxes not to be imposed save by authority of law
polity_articles.details: Mandates that no tax shall be levied or collected except by the explicit authority of law, ensuring executive accountability.
Inserted by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, it establishes a joint forum of the Centre and States to make recommendations on GST rates, exemptions, and policies.

sections.title: Economic Principles of Taxation
sections.description: Theories and classifications analyzing how tax rates affect revenue and population segments.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: Relationship between tax rates and tax revenue (Bell-shaped curve).
scientific_principles.application: Postulates that increasing tax rates beyond a certain threshold will actually decrease total tax revenue, as high rates disincentivize work, investment, and compliance.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: Tax rate increases as the taxable base amount (income) increases.
scientific_principles.application: India's Income Tax system is progressive. It shifts a heavier tax burden onto the wealthy, helping to reduce economic inequality.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: Tax burden decreases as a proportion of income as income increases.
scientific_principles.application: Indirect taxes (like GST) are inherently regressive because a poor person and a rich person pay the exact same tax amount on a commodity, taking a larger percentage of the poor person's income.

sections.title: Key Organizations and Facts
sections.description: Governing bodies associated with tax collection and important exam-oriented trivia.

key_associations.extra_info: The statutory body functioning under the Ministry of Finance responsible for administering direct tax policies like Income Tax and Corporate Tax.

key_associations.item: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC)
key_associations.extra_info: The national nodal agency responsible for formulating policies and collecting GST, Customs Duty, and Central Excise.

important_facts.fact: Income Tax was introduced for the first time in India in 1860 by Sir James Wilson to compensate for the financial losses suffered by the British regime during the Revolt of 1857.
Under Section 10(1) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, agricultural income is completely exempted from income tax in India.
